title: WhatsApp help pages told a chatbot what not to say. Meta says that is fixed
friendlyTitle: WhatsApp help pages told a chatbot what not to say. Meta says that is fixed
summary: Redact says that on 8 October it found hidden notes on 80 of 545 WhatsApp help pages, written for WhatsApp's support chatbot and not shown on screen. On the delete-account page, the note told the chatbot not to recommend a data-protection regulator. On the reporting page, once a person mentioned a lawyer or a court, the note told the chatbot not to cite privacy laws such as the GDPR, even if the person raised them. WhatsApp's European privacy policy names the right to complain to a regulator. WIRED viewed the text. WhatsApp told WIRED a bug caused it, and that the notes have been removed.
friendlySummary: Redact says that on 8 October it found hidden notes on 80 of 545 WhatsApp help pages. The notes were for WhatsApp's support chatbot. A person reading the page could not see them. On the page about deleting an account, the note told the chatbot not to suggest contacting a privacy regulator. On the page about reporting and blocking, once someone mentioned a lawyer or a court, the note told the chatbot not to mention privacy laws, even if the person brought them up. WhatsApp's own European privacy policy names the right to complain to a regulator. WhatsApp told WIRED a bug caused this, and that the notes are gone.
whyItMatters: The live pages no longer carry those notes. Redact has not shown that the chatbot followed them, or that outside assistants did. The practical point is the gap: the page a person saw and the note a model was sent were not the same page. If a support bot answers you, the public policy is still the document that states your rights. The chat is not.
